html:
Papiamento is the creole language spoken in Curacao, Aruba and Bonaire. It formed from the 1600s among enslaved Africans, Sephardic Jews and others, from Portuguese, Spanish, Dutch and African languages.

It became the everyday language of all classes, while Dutch remained the language of government. The first newspapers in Papiamento appeared in the late 1800s.

Aruba spells it Papiamento, by its Spanish roots, and Curacao and Bonaire Papiamentu, by sound. It became an official language in Aruba in 2003 and in Curacao in 2007. Its use in schools and in the labour struggles made it a symbol of island identity against Dutch rule from Willemstad.
sum: Papiamento is the creole language spoken in Curacao, Aruba and Bonaire. It formed from the 1600s among enslaved Africans, Sephardic Jews and others, from Portuguese, Spanish, Dutch and African languages.
